problem: For the original function $f(x,y,z)=xy+\arcsin z$ and point $P=(0,1,1)$, derive the level constant and the necessary range restriction separately, using the principal real arcsine. On the required band $0\le xy\le\pi$, which supplied original algebraic relation $z=\cdots$ is equivalent to $f(x,y,z)=\pi/2$? This distinct restricted-band request asks for the algebraic relation only. Explain the exact full level set and why the unrestricted relation alone would include extra points; do not claim any original choice describes the full level set without the range restriction. In verification, distinguish the revealed source algebra from its missing range restriction.
worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0,1,1) & =0\cdot 1+\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(1)=\frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ xy+\operatorname{arcsin}⁡z & =\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \operatorname{arcsin}⁡z & =\frac{\pi }{2}-xy \\ z & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-xy) \\ z & =\operatorname{cos}⁡xy\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(0,1,1)$ is the surface $z=\operatorname{cos}⁡xy.$
